html:
The Mithaka are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Channel Country of western Queensland, in today's Barcoo Shire. Their language is now extinct.

Their country lies between the Diamantina River and Cooper Creek, a land of braided channels, gibber plains and dunes. Recent archaeology carried out with Mithaka people has recorded quarries for grindstones, stone arrangements and signs of busy trade, which show a settled, organised use of the land.

Neighbours included the Yarluyandi, Karuwali, Wanggamala and Pitta Pitta. Cattle stations took the waterholes from the 1870s.
sum: The Mithaka are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Channel Country of western Queensland, in today's Barcoo Shire. Their language is now extinct.
